title: Mission reset + Team Radar: Ops guide for company-wide alignment sprint (draft)
content:
Purpose
This working doc frames a short, pragmatic alignment sprint to reset company mission emphasis and produce a single prioritized set of OKR candidates, an executive update bundle, and an all-company agenda for the next quarter. The goal: in ~9 weeks produce a clear set of decisions, owner assignments, and contingency policies that teams can implement without prolonged cross-org sloshing.

Context and why now
- Market/time: post-Series C, focus must shift from feature proliferation to predictable unit economics of inference.
- Observed symptoms: scattered launch priorities, multiple overlapping pilot projects, and inconsistent SLAs across Dedicated/Private offers.
- Outcome we want: one coherent mission statement for product/ops tradeoffs, paired with measurable OKRs that drive throughput, reliability, and cost per token.

Core artifacts to produce (deliverables)
1) Mission statement (short): one paragraph that defines the inference serving promise for the next 12 months.
2) Priority Radar: a 2x2 heatmap per theme (Reliability, Cost Efficiency, Developer Experience, Marketplace) showing impact vs. effort and risk level.
3) OKR slate (3 themes, each with 2–3 measurable key results and signal definitions).
4) Exec update packet: 2 slide executive summary + 1 page Q&A + rollout timeline.
5) All-company kickoff plan: run of show, pre-read, leader talking points, fallback FAQ.
6) Decision log and owner roster: decision ID, owner, accept criteria, rollback criteria.

Sprint cadence (9 weeks)
- Week 0 (prep): synthesize current metrics, collect 1-line POVs from each VP.
- Week 1–2 (radar & themes): product + eng + GTM workshops to map priorities into radar.
- Week 3–4 (OKR drafting): cross-functional drafting sessions producing candidate KRs with signals and measurement plan.
- Week 5 (exec review): leadership workshop to prune and endorse a 3-theme slate.
- Week 6 (comms): prepare exec packet, leader notes, and FAQ.
- Week 7 (pre-reads & dry runs): rehearsal with leaders and ops.
- Week 8 (company launch): all-company presentation + breakouts.
- Week 9 (stabilize): collect feedback, finalize decision log, schedule implementation checkpoints.

Mechanics: how to run the radar workshops
- Inputs each team must provide (by Day -3 of a workshop): 1 paragraph priority statement, 3 proposed KRs, one top risk with mitigation, and a contact owner.
- Workshop timebox: 90 minutes per theme; 45 minute mapping, 25 minute critique, 20 minute synthesis.
- Output: prioritized list of 6–8 candidate initiatives per theme and a synthesized heatmap (impact 1–5, effort 1–5, risk low/med/high).

OKR slate (early draft)
Theme A — Production Cost & Efficiency
- KR1: Reduce mean per-token serving cost by 18% across hosted workloads (measured monthly). Signal: unit cost metric by model family.
- KR2: Achieve 65% win rate for auto-quantization profiles suggested by Optimize (measured by cost delta vs. baseline).
- KR3: Reduce p95 token latency under median request size by 10% for hosted API. Signal: p95 latency over last 30 days.

Theme B — Reliability & Graceful Degradation
- KR1: < 1.5% error rate (5xx + model-fallbacks) across production routes with SLOs enabled.
- KR2: Implement and mature automatic fallback policies for top 10 routes; successful fallback response rate >= 95%.
- KR3: Increase KV cache hit rate by 20% on steady-state traffic for dedicated pools.

Theme C — Developer Experience & Adoption
- KR1: Reduce time-to-first-successful-query for new accounts from signup to first token by 40%.
- KR2: Launch three new quickstarts for common PLG patterns; adoption >= 200 orgs in first 90 days.
- KR3: Developer NPS >= 30 on new console flows.

Signal definitions and measurement notes
- Unit cost: normalized per-token cost accounting for batching and GPU hours; standard tags for route and model.
- Latency: p50/p95 measured at the gateway for each route; exclude warm-up spikes.
- Error rate: synthesized from gateway + runtime logs; fallbacks counted separately as mitigated errors.

Decision heuristics and acceptance criteria
- Decisions are accepted when 3 of 4 execs + product lead sign off OR when the data signal shows projected +10% improvement on primary KR.
- Rollback criteria: if a major customer-facing route sees >10% increase in user-facing errors for 48h, owner must pause rollout and implement fallback.

Comms plan (launch & post-launch)
- Pre-read (distributed Week 7): 2 page memo (what, why, impact, asks) + 1 page FAQ.
- All-company run of show (Week 8): 20m CEO framing, 10m product leader demo, 15m SRE status and playbook, 25m breakout Q&A with team leads.
- Post-launch: 48h digest email from leadership, public decision log link, and office hours calendar for implementation questions.

Known unknowns / open questions (to resolve in Week 1–3)
- Quantification approach for per-token cost across Dedicated vs. Hosted — single normalization or separate KRs?
- GTM enablement timeline: how quickly can Sales map existing dedicated prospects to revised SLA offers?
- Privacy/regulatory ask: what constraints change the priority of Private deployment investments?

Risks and mitigations (radar preview)
- Risk: Too many top-level KRs leading to diffusion. Mitigation: hard cap of 3 themes and max 3 KRs each.
- Risk: Measurement noise from synthetic traffic. Mitigation: cross-validate signals with production A/B and shadowing.
- Risk: Rollout coordination failure with Dedicated customers. Mitigation: pre-commit channels and customer-specific runbooks.

Quick decision table (working)
- D-001: Default quantization profiles for hosted API — owner: Sana Iqbal — timeline: W4 decision — accept when cost model projects >=12% savings without >3% quality regressions.
- D-002: Enable aggressive batching for low-latency blue routes — owner: Evan Brooks — timeline: W5 pilot — rollback if p95 latency increases >15% for >2h.

Next steps (this week)
- Ops: assemble metrics pack (owner: Miguel Sanchez) — include unit cost by model family, p95 latency by route, recent error taxonomy. Due: 2025-01-17.
- VPs: 1-line POVs due to company-ops slack channel by 2025-01-16.
- Product: draft radar templates and workshop facilitator notes (owner: Karen Liu). Due: 2025-01-14.

Notes to self / meeting prep cues
- Keep workshop output visual and short — no more than 4 radar items per slide.
- Emphasize owner-level accountability in the decision log (names + escalation path).
- Prepare fallback language for leader scripts: "if we need to pivot, here's the rollback path and customer notice template."

Appendix (links to starter exhibits)
- Current metric snapshot: linked in linked_artifacts.
- Example radar image: template in design repo (see github link).

Document history
- 2025-01-10: initial draft authored (Karen Liu).
- 2025-01-12: added early OKR candidates and sprint timeline (collaborators: Evan, Sana).
- 2025-01-15: updated risks and decision heuristics after exec sync.

End of working draft.

(Use this doc as the single source for workshop prep; when we lock decisions, we will copy final artifacts into Confluence and publish the executive packet.)
